note: Multi-turn follow-up cases for ADR-0013. `turns` are spoken in order; only the LAST is scored. `expect` is the tool call the last turn should produce, or null for a decline. `restate` marks the declines that must specifically ask for restatement rather than apologise. Cases marked `negative` are the ones memory must NOT resolve - they carry the failure this feature is priced at, and a run that resolves them all is worse than one that misses a few follow-ups.
model_note: A `model` block overrides `expect`/`restate` when a model-backed router is scored, because the two routers are allowed to differ and one of them is allowed to be better. The deterministic stub defers a mangled entity (ADR-0016 says the model has the sentence context to resolve it, and it does); and `needs_restatement` is a stub concept the tool APIs cannot express, so a model decline is scored on being a decline, not on carrying the flag. Where a `model` block records something WORSE, it is a limitation and says so.
